summary: The AI Engineer World's Fair 2024 Open Models track opens with a music intro, then transitions to the 'Codgen' (code generation) sub-track. Britney Walker, a GP at Charles River Ventures (CRV)—a 54-year-old early-stage VC investing at seed and Series A—introduces three speakers: Rahul Pandita from GitHub (Copilot Workspaces), Kevin from Codium, and Michael from Cursor, with Pandita leading off. Pandita describes GitHub Next as approximately 20 senior researchers, developers, and tool builders who work outside the regular product organization and report directly to the CEO. Their charter is to explore the future of software engineering, with emphasis on 'explore' because the future is genuinely unknown. Successful explorations are handed off to product and development teams to become products like Copilot. To frame the current AI moment, Pandita invokes Andrew Ng's analogy that AI is 'the new electricity.' He parallels factory electrification: before the 1880s, factories were architected around giant centrally-located steam engines with belt-and-pulley systems—technology dictated workflow. Electric motors arrived in the 1880s, retaining efficiency at small scale, yet mainstream adoption took until the 1920s—a roughly 40-year period of exploration and de-risking. Pandita positions GitHub Next's work in an analogous exploration phase. The exploration pipeline follows progressive stages: a functional prototype is dogfooded within the Next team, then across the company, then released as a tech preview to early adopters, and potentially becomes a product. Projects can be killed or shelved at any stage.
